thesis: Monster Beverage is executing its strongest growth phase in a decade: Q1 2026 net sales rose 26.9% to $2.35B (first $2B+ quarter in company history, an 8.9% beat), adjusted EPS +23.7% to $0.58, and international sales grew 44.9% to ~45% of revenue on Coca-Cola's distribution network plus China/India demand. New products launched since September 2025 already contribute ~15% of US sales. The business is high quality and net cash, but the stock has re-rated hard (+31.6% in 90 days to ~$95-97, ~47x trailing earnings) and now trades at or above the FactSet mean target of $93.55, so the growth is largely priced in. A 2-for-1 stock split is effective August 10, 2026.
catalysts: Q2 2026 earnings (~August 2026): continuation of the 25%+ international-led growth would force further estimate revisions
Two-for-one stock split effective August 10, 2026 (announced; retail-flow tailwind)
Management projection of ~$10B revenue by FY2027 (vs a FY2025 base implied by prior-year Q1 net sales of $1.85B) - hitting the glidepath re-rates the growth narrative
New product wave: brands launched since Sep 2025 already ~15% of US sales (Morgan Stanley, July 2026)
Ongoing buyback: ~$400M remaining authorized after ~$100M repurchased in Q1 2026 at avg $73.86
risk_factors: Valuation: ~47x trailing P/E and price ($96.87 at pass1 snapshot) already above the FactSet mean analyst target of $93.55 - little margin for execution slip
Gross margin compressed to 55.0% from 56.5% y/y on geographic mix, aluminum can costs, and freight - international mix shift is structurally margin-dilutive
Growth increasingly tied to international expansion, raising exposure to regulatory shifts, tariffs, and local demand shocks (China, India)
FCF conversion lags the P&L: FY2025 FCF was $1.97B (~$2.08/share TTM as of Mar 2026), so the stock trades near ~47x FCF as well
Energy-drink category regulatory risk (caffeine limits, youth-marketing restrictions) is a persistent Low-probability/High-impact overhang
